rows.why: Drawing is unique to this option and shows BOTH trouser back pockets as a welt plus a pointed/diamond flap with a central buttonhole. Measured apex-drop/flap-width on the flap bottom edge, a ratio along the same surface so hip foreshortening largely cancels. Drawing red components: left 58/335=0.173, right 56/335=0.167. Photo: left flap x95-323 (w=228) apex y=422 vs corners y=384/379, drop 40 -> 0.175; right flap x557-797 (w=240) apex y=429 vs corners 383/391, drop 42 -> 0.175. Agreement within 1-5%, and the slight inflation is the expected direction for a curved hip. Count matches (2 pockets), button sits at the point on both.

Drawing is unique to this option and shows the trouser back with BOTH pockets highlighted as horizontal welts, each carrying a small perpendicular tick at the OUTER end - the zipper pull. The photo matches on every countable feature: two welt pockets, both fitted with a visible contrast zipper (so the zipper is positively demonstrated, not implied), and the pull tab sits at the OUTER end of each pocket - left pocket pull at the left/outer end, right pocket pull at the right/outer end - reproducing the drawing's tick placement rather than mirroring it. Count, type and hardware orientation all agree; nothing about the row's claim is left unsettled.

Drawing 0101__Normal shows a straight welt chest pocket but is shared by cp-welt-23/25/27. The photo's welt is confirmed geometrically STRAIGHT: welt slot traced over a verified 316px span (x340-656, n=80, outlier-rejected at 12px), slope -9.52 deg rising toward the armhole, quadratic sagitta +0.15px = 0.05% of span. That confirms the drawn shape and separates it from the curved (0102__Arc) and boat (0103) siblings, which carry their own drawings. DISCARDED READING: a first pass with an unconstrained y-window put the endpoints at x=320->y=652 and x=680->y=686, both off the welt, yielding a spurious -24.96px sagitta; refitting on the verified span removed it. The 2.3 vs 2.5 vs 2.7 cm depth is encoded nowhere and no cm figure is recoverable.

Drawing 3406 is unique to this option; its red overlay traces the waistband edge then the fly topstitch curving down to a pointed terminus rather than a squared-off bartack. In the photo I traced the topstitch as the strongest local darkness deficit per row: (550,675), (575,666), (625,645), (675,618), (750,559), (775,533), (800,502), (825,470), (850,438), (875,416) - a clean monotonic curve converging onto the centre-front seam at x~406 by y~900, i.e. a pointed convergence with no horizontal bar. CONTROL: the same tracer on fly-straight.webp stays locked at x~450 for the entire 300-975 range, confirming the measurement discriminates curved-pointed from straight. Not measured: fly-french and fly-fish-claw as additional controls, hence medium confidence.

Double source failure. (1) The illustration /images/jacket/lining/half-lining.jpg is a BUTTON/THREAD COLOUR CHART - a grid of colour tiles labelled YZ063, 124, YZ001 - not a lining construction drawing. (2) That same path is shared verbatim by hls-half, hls-third-cutaway and hls-quarter-cutaway. The photo does show a genuinely part-lined jacket interior (lining across upper chest/shoulders and side panels, unlined lower back with taped centre seam and cross-stitching). The three sibling photos are byte-distinct (eb0dd75b78 / f430c921be / f11b992816) so they are not literally reused, but nothing in the source can establish which is 1/2 vs 1/3 vs 1/4 cut-away.

Drawing 0689__Notch_with_high_gorge is UNIQUE to this option (not shared), and the photo does show a notch lapel with a visibly high gorge, so the family is right and it is not WRONG. But the defining 68 deg claim is unverifiable. On the drawing's right side I located the notch vertex at ~(838,314) where the collar-leaf outer edge and the gorge seam converge, with the collar tip at ~(860,290) and the lapel point at ~(884,352), giving a notch OPENING of ~87 deg. I explicitly did NOT report the gorge-seam inclination (the separate diagonal run from (746,248) to (840,314)) as the notch angle. The notch arms are only 35-50px long while the ink is 12-16px thick, so uncertainty is about +/-20 deg - that neither confirms nor refutes 68. Gorge HEIGHT could not be normalised either: the drawing is a lapel-only abstract with no shoulder, armhole or chest landmark shared with the photograph.

Shared-drawing source problem. The illustration path ec013dda688e__0002__Peak.jpg is the identical file used by ELEVEN peak options (101, 102, 102-rl, 103-curved, 105, 107, 108, 110, 110-low, 115, 120-curved); peak-99 and peak-114 instead use 0004__Semi-peak. It is a generic style diagram carrying no printed angle callout, so it cannot specify 102 degrees. The photo does show a true peak lapel with the peaks sweeping up above the gorge, so the style FAMILY matches the drawing and is distinguishable from notch and shawl. But 102 vs 101 vs 105 vs 107 is not separable from this source, and I deliberately did not manufacture a degree figure from an assumed lapel size.

Shared-drawing source problem: b795127dc02f__02A1__Regular_slanted.jpg is the identical path for six options (slanted-flap 40/45/50/55/60/65). The drawing shows both hip pockets as slanted flaps, the flap parallelogram rising toward the side seam. The photo does show a slanted flap hip pocket with that same rise direction, so it matches the drawn family and is distinguishable from the straight 0201__Regular and the besom 0231 siblings. The 6.0 cm flap depth is not encoded in the drawing and carries no dimension callout, so it cannot be confirmed. Sibling photos in this group are byte-distinct, so no literal reuse at this row.

Shared-drawing source problem compounded by a non-photographable property. 9fd6de75414f__060K__Regular.jpg is the identical path for pad-01, pad-03, pad-05-soft and pad-05-structured, and its only mark is a small red triangle at the outer shoulder indicating the pad build zone - no thickness callout. The photo is a shoulder/sleevehead close-up, so the control region is correctly in frame and unobstructed. But +0.5cm cannot be separated from +0.3 or +0.1 without a shared validated landmark, and soft vs structured is an internal canvas/handle difference that a finished-garment exterior shot cannot express at all. Four options, one drawing, one indistinguishable exterior view.

Proved the source cannot encode this option: the three pleat-depth drawings 302Z (1.5cm), 302H (2.0cm) and 302E (2.5cm) are BYTE-IDENTICAL - all md5 cff5d24b5a38983d3cae4d2ac9573aa5, max absolute pixel difference 0 between them, identical red overlays (6195 px, bbox x295-805 y60-516, inset callout 76px). Three filenames, one image. Separately, pleat depth is the fabric folded under and is not visible on a finished trouser front. DISCARDED READING: sustained-vertical-fold scoring over y260-620 gave pleat-15 a peak of 16.2 at x=549, but flat-front.webp scored higher (34.2 at x=139) where that column is the leg silhouette edge, so the metric does not discriminate pleated from flat and I am not resting anything on it.

The defining feature is buttons arranged in doubled pairs down the front placket rather than evenly spaced singles. Upscaling the drawing shows one collar button at the placket top followed by five tightly-spaced PAIRS. The photo shows the same construction: a neck button, then three complete pairs (two buttons nearly touching, ~50px apart, with ~300px between groups) plus the first button of a fourth pair at the bottom crop line. That grouping is unmistakable and cannot be confused with siblings btn-6/7/8/9, which are all single-button plackets. Confidence is medium only because the mid-chest crop cuts off groups 4 and 5, so the literal count of five is inferred rather than seen; the visible spacing is consistent with five, and nothing contradicts the drawing. Noted but not disqualifying: the buttons are sewn with red cross-stitch thread, which literalizes the drawing's red annotation markers - a styling quirk, not a construction mismatch.

Drawing carries a printed 85.00 degree callout with leader arrows onto the two collar point tips; the callout convention was independently validated on french-in-8cm (printed 145, drawing measured 151). Drawing shows pointed tips, no tip buttons, one band button; photo matches on family and button configuration. Photo spread off a 50px-gridded render: vertex (405,505), tips (250,690) and (625,665), giving 40 and 54 degree half-angles, total 94 vs drawn 85. The 14 degree asymmetry shows the model is rotated off-axis so this is 94 plus or minus 10. Across all ten leafed photos measured the same way the apparent-spread ranking matched the drawn-callout ranking monotonically. DEFECT: necktie plus fastened throat button completely conceal the collar band.

Button count contradiction. At 16x nearest-neighbour raw-pixel zoom of both collar leaves, button-down-collar-with-78cm-stand.jpg has NO button anywhere on either leaf; its only button is a single throat button on the band, inside the triangular gap where the leaves cross. The convention is verified inside the family: point-in-7cm-with-button.jpg, at identical scale and viewpoint, draws a distinct 4px circle on each leaf just above the tip PLUS the throat button, so this illustrator does draw tip buttons when they exist. The photo shows tip buttons on BOTH points (left ~(320,720), right ~(755,715), each confirmed at 4x) and hides the band and its throat button entirely behind a necktie. The photo adds two buttons the drawing lacks and conceals the one it has. Secondary and weaker: the drawing prints 90.00 degrees and measures ~95 as drawn, while the photo projects 76.9 degrees with a 5.9 degree left/right asymmetry as the error bar. ESCALATE THE DRAWING TOO: a file named button-down-collar that draws no button-down is a source defect. Also note 7.8 cm is not a plausible collar-stand height - real stands run 3-4.5 cm - so that number looks like a point length mis-filed as a stand.

Drawing: 115.00 degree callout, pointed tips, NO tip buttons. Photo shows sharp-pointed tips, clean and bare - correctly distinguished from collar-cutaway-55-btn, its only real sibling (the two illustrations differ by ink-region mean 20.2, attributable to the two tip buttons alone). Measured spread: vertex (400,490), tips (140,655) and (660,640), 57.6 and 60.0, total 118 against drawn 115 - closest agreement of the three 115 degree options. COULD NOT MEASURE: the 5.5 cm point length. This matters because cutaway-55 and large-cutaway-75 carry the SAME 115 degree callout and are separated in the catalog only by point length, which no drawing prints.

Drawing: 115.00 degree callout plus two small circles at the collar point tips (button-down). Photo shows exactly two buttons, one at each collar point tip at (130,600) and (655,605), plus the band button - count and placement match. Spread from vertex (395,495) to tips (110,640) and (680,640): 63.0 degrees each side, perfectly symmetric so the subject is square to camera, total 126 against a drawn 115. Reads 11 degrees wide but is unambiguously in the widest non-french class and comfortably wider than the 100/105 degree photos measured identically (99, 101). Separation from its no-button twin rests entirely on the tip buttons and they are plainly visible and correctly counted. COULD NOT MEASURE: 5.5 cm point length, no printed length callout anywhere in this family.

The one option where the drawing itself was measured rather than the callout trusted. On a common scale the drawn crossover vertex sits at (378,425) with leaf tips at (155,485) and (600,480), giving half-angles 74.9 and 76.1 - a drawn spread of 151 against the printed 145. That validates the callout convention for the whole shirt-collar family. Photo: vertex (300,580), tips (95,700) and (640,700), total 130. The 11 degree left/right asymmetry shows the subject is rotated, and horizontal foreshortening of a collar across a curved chest compresses apparent spread, so 130 for a 145 flat drawing errs in the expected direction and magnitude. Strongest check: measured by one identical method this is the widest of all ten leafed photographs and its drawing is the widest of all ten drawings, by a large margin in both.

Drawing shows a full TURNDOWN collar with two large angular leaves - traced on a 900px render each leaf has a top-inner corner, an outer wing point reaching past the shoulder/yoke lines, an upward notch apex and a centre-front point, six exterior vertices across the pair. The photo shows an upright band/stand collar with NO leaves at all. Quantified against the neck-opening width at the collar top edge, validated first as comparable (290px drawing vs 270px photo on a common render): the drawn collar lowest point sits 1.62 neck-widths below its top edge, the photographed collar 0.80 - roughly half as deep. Vertical foreshortening on a near-frontal chest accounts for 1.0-1.2x, nowhere near 2x. The photo matches the option LABEL and description but the drawing is the authority.

Drawing: 115.00 degree callout, pointed tips, no tip buttons; photo matches family and button configuration. Measured spread: vertex (355,468), tips (85,660) and (700,690), half-angles 54.6 and 57.2, total 112 against drawn 115. Sits in the correct band relative to same-method measurements of the 100/105 degree photos (99, 101) below and french (130) above. COULD NOT MEASURE: the 7.5 cm point length, the sole catalog discriminator between this and collar-cutaway-55 since both are drawn at 115 degrees. Here the band button, the only plausible shared scale landmark, is hidden behind the tie knot. Raw pixel lengths across photos at different framings are meaningless and were not used.

Drawing: 105.00 degree callout, pointed tips, no tip buttons; photo matches family. Measured spread: vertex (395,480), tips (195,660) and (605,640), half-angles 48.0 and 52.7, total 101 against drawn 105. First visual impression from the contact sheet was that this looked too narrow for a large cut-away; measuring corrected that impression, which is why the measurement is reported rather than the impression. COULD NOT MEASURE: the 8.0 cm point length, the only thing separating this from its 115 degree siblings. Normalising point length by neck width across photos was attempted and discarded - each photo uses a different model at different framing and the resulting ratios inverted the label order, so the landmark did not validate.

The drawing cannot settle this. large-round-in-53cm.jpg and round-in-53cm.jpg are different files but effectively the same drawing: resampled to a common 300x300 and differenced over the ink region only, mean absolute difference is 16.9/255 - LOWER than the 20.2 measured between cut-away-in-55cm and its with-button twin, whose only genuine difference is two 4px tip buttons. Both carry identical 100.00 degree callouts and both labels say 5.3 cm. Confirmed: the photo shows a club collar with fully rounded tips, no points, band button visible - correct family. Cannot confirm which of the two round options it is. Angle reading discarded: a club collar has no sharp front-edge crossing so the vertex is ill-defined. This is a catalog spec defect, not an image defect - no regeneration can fix it.

Drawing: 90.00 degree callout, pointed tips, NO tip buttons - which is what separates it from collar-mid-cutaway-70-btn, whose drawing is identical apart from two small circles at the tips. Photo shows pointed tips with no tip buttons, correct. Measured spread: vertex (395,597), tips (295,690) and (500,685), about 96 against a drawn 90. Least confident reading in the batch: the tips sit low in frame against a dark suit so tip localisation is soft by about 25px, i.e. 10 degrees. Note this option and collar-af1-70 are drawn only 5 degrees apart, below photographic resolution, so that pair is not distinguishable regardless of image.

Drawing: 90.00 degree callout plus two small circles at the collar point tips. Photo shows exactly two white buttons, one anchoring each collar point tip, plus the band button; count and placement match. Spread from vertex (400,395) to tips (100,700) and (700,690): 44.5 and 45.5 degree half-angles, total 90 - the closest agreement with a drawn callout in the batch, and the near-perfect symmetry means the model is square to camera so no rotation correction is needed. NOTE: the catalog description says a throat button, which the drawing contradicts - the drawing shows tip buttons. The drawing wins and the photograph follows it, so the description is what needs fixing.

The drawing filed for this row shows a plain band/stand collar with one throat button, NO tab and NO collar leaves - the same artwork as rolled-stand-collar.jpg at 1.64/255 mean absolute difference. The photo agrees with that drawing: band collar, single silver stud at the band base, no leaves, no tab. So photo and drawing match, but they match on something that is not a one-piece 7.5 cm collar with tab. A tab is a large unmistakable feature - a fabric strap crossing behind the knot - and it is absent from BOTH. Because the drawing is the authority and has no tab, the photo cannot be called WRONG; but the drawing is almost certainly mis-filed, since its own length-siblings one-piece-collar-in-85cm-with-tab.jpg and -9cm-with-tab.jpg are visibly different artwork with a different viewpoint, vertical CF placket and offset button.

This drawing is the outlier of its family: oblique skewed projection, NO printed angle callout where its three siblings all print 60.00 degrees, and the left collar leaf drawn turned up. At 22x nearest-neighbour zoom a ~5px ring is drawn at the LEFT collar point only; no button is drawn at the right point. The photo shows a long point collar with a white 4-hole button and buttonhole at the LEFT point and a completely BARE right point, verified at 4x on crop x640-880/y600-780. Projected spread, apex at the leaf crossing (555,350) to tips (318,715) and (770,700), is 33.0 + 31.6 = 64.6 degrees with only 1.4 degrees left/right asymmetry. Two readings remain and the drawing cannot settle them: either the photo faithfully copies a drawing that itself exposes one button, or the intended option is a two-tip button-down like all three callout-bearing siblings and the photo is missing the right button. DEFECT either way: the left/right button asymmetry is not a real garment, and the band is hidden by a necktie.

The photo matches its drawing on every feature: band/stand collar, no leaves, one white 4-hole button at the band base, softly rolled top edge, band fully visible with no necktie. What blocks a pass is sibling separation, not photo quality. rolled-stand-collar.jpg is effectively the SAME artwork as one-piece-collar-in-75cm-with-tab.jpg - mean absolute pixel difference 1.64/255 at native size, only 1.6% of pixels differing by more than 40, and those differences are 1px shifts on the CF seam and inner band edge visible in a red/cyan overlay - and near-identical to one-piece-collar-in-8cm-with-tab.jpg at 2.93/255. Three catalog options share one drawing. COULD NOT MEASURE: band height - no length callout on any of the three drawings, and scaling from the photo would require assuming a real-world garment size.

Same root cause as collar-large-round-53: the two source drawings are pixel-equivalent over the ink region (mean diff 16.9/255), carry identical 100 degree callouts, and both labels state 5.3 cm, so the illustration cannot adjudicate which photo belongs to which option. Confirmed on this one: club collar with fully rounded tips and no points, band button visible. Its spread does measure cleanly - vertex (400,465), rounded tip bottoms (185,630) and (590,645), giving 52.5 and 46.5 degree half-angles, total 99 against the drawn 100. So the image is consistent with its own drawing; it simply is not separable from its sibling.

Drawing shows a band-only mandarin stand collar: no leaves, band front ends cut square, a narrow vertical gap between the band ends at centre front, a small step where the band meets the shirt front. No angle callout, correctly, since spread is undefined for a band collar. Photo matches on every structural point including the square-cut ends that separate it from the rounded-stand sibling in the same techpack folder. Critically this is one of only two images in the batch photographed with NO necktie and the throat open, so the band - the entire discriminating feature - is fully visible. NOTE: the catalog description contradicts the drawing, describing collar points cut with a squared-off end, i.e. a squared POINT collar. The drawing shows no points at all; the description needs fixing.

The defining feature is two buttons stacked vertically on a tall rounded collar stand (both marked in red at centre front). The photo shows a standard-height band carrying a single visible button at the throat, with the second button position covered by a necktie knot; the button count that defines this option is not depicted and the visible stand reads as an ordinary one-button band rather than a tall round two-button stand.

I contrast-boosted the file to hunt for the armhole and there is no armhole seam, no sleeve cap, and no set-in sleeve anywhere in the frame; the sleeve head is entirely off-camera. The showcased feature is absent and the image depicts a different garment part. [upheld on skeptical re-check: Verified independently. The drawing's red highlight runs from the neck point along the shoulder and then arcs outward past the body silhouette as the sleeve-cap contour; that arc is the only thing that distinguishes a sleeve-head option. Drawing calls for the same 1.0 cm transverse bar but only 1.5 cm back from the collar point opening edge; photo places the red bar hard against the front/point end of the leaf, distinctly closer to the tip than the 4 cm variant, so the offset ordering between the two options is preserved.

Drawing callout shows a 1.0 cm transverse bar set back 4 cm from the collar point opening edge, crossing the full leaf from fold to lower edge; photo shows one dark-red bar of that width crossing the leaf at roughly mid-leaf, clearly set back from the point, and mirrored on the opposite leaf.

Drawing shows two parallel contrast stripes flanking both edges of the front placket; photo shows exactly two red vertical stripes, one on each placket edge, running the full length past the collar button and the next button - count of two verified, not one and not three.

Drawing fills the lower half of each top-collar leaf with contrast while the upper/fold edge stays base cloth; photo shows navy occupying the lower diagonal band of both leaves down to the points with white along the top fold edge, matching the split direction.

Drawing marks only the 0.6 cm collar point opening edges - the two front edges forming the V from tip up to the stand - with no contrast on the outer/lower collar edge; photo shows exactly that: thin red piping on both opening edges only, outer leaf edges and points left plain white.

Drawing shows exactly one contrast stripe running vertically down the left edge of the front placket; photo shows a single navy stripe on one placket edge only, with the opposite placket edge plain - stripe count of one confirmed at high zoom past two buttons.

Drawing specifies a single narrow 1.0 cm strip running lengthwise through the middle of the top collar, interrupted at the centre-front V; photo shows one narrow slate-blue strip of roughly one-centimetre width tracking the collar mid-band on both leaves and stopping at the inner leaf corners - one strip, not an edge trim or a full panel.

Drawing traces a 0.6 cm contrast edge around the entire top collar outline - down the opening edge to the point and back along the outer/lower leaf edge toward the shoulders; photo shows continuous red edge trim on both segments of both leaves, distinguishing it correctly from the point-opening-only option.

Drawing shows a small solid 2 cm contrast triangle at each of the two collar point tips and nowhere else; photo shows one red triangular patch at each collar point tip, both leaves, with the rest of the collar plain white - shape, count and location all match.

Drawing puts the contrast on the upper portion of the top collar adjacent to the fold/neck with the point region left in base cloth; photo shows blue along the top fold edge of both leaves running to the back neck, with white at the collar points - inverse of the lower-part option, as required.

Drawing shows dashed stitch outlines at both point areas plus No Felling Stitch, i.e. a stay permanently sewn inside. The photo shows a closed stitched stay channel consistent with a fixed stay, but also an unexplained button plus buttonhole slit on the collar leaf appearing nowhere in the drawing, which could equally read as a removable-stay opening; fixed-versus-removable cannot be settled from this frame.

The drawing's printed callout reads 0.6cm, contradicting the row's 0.1 cm label, and the drawing wins. This is also the only drawing in the family rendered at 221x221 rather than 192x192, so its offsets are not directly comparable to siblings without rescaling. The photo does show a tonal stitch line inset from the leaf edge and turning the point, so the stitching is present on the correct part. But neither discriminator resolves: offset in cm is unmeasurable (no scale landmark in the photo, and the drawings do not encode offset to scale), and the AMF-versus-machine distinction is not readable - at 6x on a 160px crop this stitch's pitch, length and regularity are indistinguishable from the machine siblings, with none of the long widely spaced slightly irregular pick stitches that make AMF identifiable, as they obviously are in stitch-03-amf.

Two blockers, both in the source data. First, machine-01cm-top-stitching.jpg is BYTE-IDENTICAL to machine-03cm-top-stitching.jpg (md5 8e910bc6bbdd1d964c7e92557800de00, 8241 bytes each), so 0.1 cm and 0.3 cm cannot be told apart. Second, the drawing's printed callout reads 0.3cm, contradicting the row label, and the drawing wins. Tested whether the drawn offset encodes the printed number by measuring the red stitch line offset from the collar edge on the right leaf across the family, all normalised to 192x192: printed 0.1cm gives 4px, 0.3cm gives 4px, 0.5cm gives 5px, 0.6cm gives 4px. The drawn offsets do NOT scale with the printed values, so those two measurements disagree and neither is validated - unlike the collar-angle callouts, these stitching drawings do not encode their dimension to scale. The photo does show the right feature class: a fine tonal machine topstitch parallel to and inset from the leaf edge.

The drawing's printed callout reads 0.1cm, contradicting the row's 0.3 cm label, and the drawing wins. The photo is the only one in the batch showing a genuine AMF signature - long, widely spaced, slightly irregular pick stitches following the leaf edge and mitring round the point - so the construction class reads correctly and is distinguishable from the machine group. Two problems stop it passing. The offset is unverifiable for the same reason as the rest of the family. And the stitches are rendered in RED contrast thread while all seven siblings are tonal white-on-white; red is the drafting convention every one of these drawings uses to highlight the stitch line, so the photo appears to have literalised an annotation colour as real thread. Since thread colour is a separate option group in this catalog, a customer would read this photo as a thread-colour choice rather than a stitch-offset choice.

Same drawing file as stitch-01-top, byte-identical at md5 8e910bc6bbdd1d964c7e92557800de00, so the two options cannot be separated by their illustrations. Here the printed callout 0.3cm does agree with the row label. The photo shows a fine continuous tonal machine topstitch inset from the outer edge of both leaves and turning both points - correct feature class and garment part. But the discriminating dimension is the offset and it is unmeasurable: the drawing does not encode offset to scale (4px for 0.1cm, 4px for 0.3cm, 5px for 0.5cm, 4px for 0.6cm at 192x192) and the photograph carries no scale landmark.

This is the only drawing in the family carrying NO callout at all and no detail-bubble inset - it just draws a dense red zigzag along the leaf edge, so there is no printed dimension to hold the photo to. Whether that zigzag is meant to sit ON the edge at offset zero or is merely a bolder rendering of the same nominal line cannot be decided: by eye it rides the edge, but the same automated offset scan that returns 5px for the printed-0.5cm top-stitch drawing also returns 5px here, so the two readings disagree and neither is validated. The photo shows a tonal stitch line clearly INSET from the leaf edge with ordinary machine pitch and no readable AMF signature, so it neither confirms the drawing's edge-riding zigzag nor its AMF class, and there is no quantitative content in the drawing to check it against.

machine-05cm-top-stitching.jpg is BYTE-IDENTICAL to machine-06cm-top-stitching.jpg (md5 7a75c65c1f4fb2cbbea798f622252ab5, 8227 bytes each), so 0.5 and 0.6 cm share one drawing. The printed callout reads 0.5cm, agreeing with this row. The photo shows a tonal machine topstitch inset from the leaf edge - right feature class and part - and by eye its inset looks the widest of the four top-stitch photos, but that will not be converted to cm: the drawing does not encode offset to scale, and the photos are framed at different zooms with no shared landmark, so cross-photo pixel offsets are not comparable.

Same drawing file as stitch-05-top (md5 7a75c65c1f4fb2cbbea798f622252ab5), and its printed callout reads 0.5cm, contradicting this row's 0.6 cm label with the drawing winning. So the drawing both contradicts the label and is shared with a sibling. The photo shows a tonal stitch line parallel to and inset from the leaf edge and turning the point - right feature class. DISCARDED READING recorded: the stitch character initially read as a discrete hand/pick stitch rather than a machine line, but on a matched 6x zoom against 01-top, 03-top, 05-top, 01-amf and 05-amf every one resolves into discrete stitches at that magnification, so beaded-versus-continuous is not a valid discriminator at this resolution.

The illustration this row points at is a 300x300 grey placeholder card bearing the literal word None rather than a technical drawing, but the parallel techpack file images/techpacks/shirt/decoration_stitching_on_collar/none.jpg draws the intent properly: a collar whose leaf edge is plain and unstitched in the detail bubble. The photo shows a point collar whose leaf edges are completely clean, no stitch line on either leaf, checked at 2x on the left-leaf crop (80,150)-(480,550) and on the full frame. Unambiguously separable from all seven siblings, every one of which draws a stitch line along the leaf edge. Absence is the entire spec and absence is what the photo shows.

BROKEN SOURCE ASSET. The illustration /images/jacket/chest-dart/minus-2.jpg is a 240x200 crop of a BUTTON catalogue page (four buttons captioned FK763621 and BK73/FKE03233), not a chest-dart drawing. I checked the whole directory: all five siblings (minus-2, minus-3, standard, plus-2, plus-3) have distinct sha256 hashes but every one is a button-swatch tile (codes FKE003204 RED PATTERN WOVEN, NJ34/FK3132BN HORN, GS15/FK283214 COROZO). Label "No Heel Guard". Photo is a clean pressed trouser hem with a turned edge and NO guard, tape, ribbon or reinforcing patch anywhere on the hem circumference. Absence is the feature and absence is what is depicted; it is also clearly distinguishable from all three siblings, which each carry a visible guard.

Label "Whole Circle (Finished Ribbon)". Photo shows a pale contrast ribbon running the entire hem circumference, finished along both long edges with a dark bound edge — the "finished ribbon" treatment that distinguishes this from the plain whole-circle guard. Full-width coverage and the bound finish are both present, and no annotation colour appears.

Label "Heel Guard". Photo shows a single self-fabric reinforcing patch stitched to the back portion of the hem only — a clearly bounded rectangle with its own topstitched outline, occupying part of the hem circumference rather than all of it. That partial coverage is exactly what separates this option from the two whole-circle siblings.

ANNOTATION RENDERED INTO A CUSTOMER-FACING PHOTO. The guard band runs the full hem width (correct for "Whole Circle"), but it is enclosed by a bright RED outline on all four sides. Red is the tech-pack highlight colour used to mark the feature being specified — it is manufacturing documentation, not garment construction, and must never appear in a shipped photograph (standing rule; same defect already logged for trousers/hem-machine-plain). Confirmed as annotation bleed rather than a design feature by the sibling heel-ribbon, whose equivalent whole-circle band is bound in black self-fabric with no red anywhere. Construction is otherwise plausible, so this needs a regeneration with the red suppressed, not a re-interpretation.

Drawing knot-dash shows a VERTICAL pocket whose end callout carries only a SHORT dash, clearly shorter than the mouth width and offset to one side, in deliberate contrast to knot-i whose bar spans the full mouth. Orientation and the short one-sided form both match, and it is visibly a different construction from the knot-i photo. Drawing knot-hip-i shows a HORIZONTAL hip pocket - the callout draws both welt lips as horizontal lines - with a vertical I bar at the pocket end spanning the full height across both lips. knot-i shows a VERTICAL pocket with a straight bar of stitching running the FULL WIDTH across the mouth at its end, edge to edge. DEFECT not reconciled: the tack is rendered in bright RED thread, whereas red in this drawing set is the highlight convention marking the graded feature - the same red marks the seam in 3130, the welt in 3132 and the stripe in 3121. The generator appears to have literalised the highlight as thread colour. Not failed on it because the graded attribute is tack GEOMETRY, which is correct.

Verified the discriminator is real by reading the sibling notch-lapel-vest.webp ('Notch without Collar Band'): unmistakably a sleeveless vest over shirt and tie whose notch lapel runs straight to the shoulder seam with NO collar behind the neck at all. Held at medium confidence for three reasons I could not resolve: the crop cuts off the armhole so vest-vs-jacket is not provable from this frame, the model is bare-chested (unusual styling for a vest neckline), and whether the collar is a separate stand or a one-piece collar cannot be resolved at this resolution.

Drawing (/images/options/vest/notch-lapel-vest.jpg) shows a waistcoat neckline with a notch cut at each side (a clear step where the collar leaf meets the lapel at y~300-350), lapels running to a deep V that terminates at a single small button at (540,1010), and no separate collar stand strip at the neckline. Photo satisfies all three discriminators. (1) Garment: sleeveless - the armhole edge with the white shirt sleeve behind it is visible at the image-left margin, so it is a waistcoat, not a jacket. (2) Notch: at 1.9x on the neck region (x80-760, y80-420) the collar leaf point and the lapel's top corner form an outward-opening V gap on both sides; the lapel does not rise above the collar, so it is a notch and not a peak, and there is no continuous uninterrupted spline, so not a shawl - this also rules out v-neckline and u-neckline, which have no lapel at all. (3) Collar band: absence positively demonstrated, not cropped - the whole neck and both shoulder tops are in frame and no strip of waistcoat cloth stands up behind the shirt collar, which is what separates this row from lapel-collar-stand. V terminates at a single button at (425,995), matching the drawing. Not measurable: the drawing carries no callout, so the description's 6-8 cm lapel width is not recoverable; my attempt to derive it from the drawn neck-point span (295 px) gave ~4.7 cm on an assumed neck width and I am discarding that as manufactured.

The neckline itself checks out. Drawing shows a waistcoat neckline with a collar band, collar leaves and lapels ending in sharp outward peaks breaking to one low button. Gradient maps of both lapel tops in the photo show a sharp outer corner with the lapel's top edge running horizontally inboard to the gorge (left: horizontal edge y~224 from x=100 to x=200, outer point at x~100; right mirrored, y~220 from x=702 to x=810) and NO V gap - whereas the notch sibling notch-lapel-vest.webp mapped the same way shows an unmistakable V between collar point and lapel point. So it is peak-family and distinguishable from the notch and shawl siblings. What I could NOT settle: whether the garment is a waistcoat at all. The armhole/shoulder-strap edge that defines a vest is out of frame, and the shirt here is navy so the usual value cue is gone. Texture test at the frame edges gives high-frequency sd 21.7 for the far-left strip vs 21.8 for the known garment body and 10.8 for the navy shirt - i.e. hopsack, not shirt, runs to the left frame edge at chest height, whereas in the notch vest control the shirt is visible from x~95 outward. That points to a jacket body rather than a waistcoat but the crops differ enough that I will not call it. Circumstantial: this row and the other two collar-band vest options are filed under generated/suit-3pc/, while the band-less vest options sit under generated/vest/.
